setup_name: London Kill Zone — Pre-Open Momentum Sweep

setup_name: London-New York Overlap — Peak Volume Window

setup_name: Asian-London Transition — Range Breakout Setup

This 'failure swing' setup has a 65-70% win rate when combined with higher timeframe trend direction. setup_name: Post-NY Lunch Drift — Low Probability Zone

setup_name: NY Afternoon Push — Trend Continuation or Reversal

Key signal: if the morning established a clear trend AND the 12:00-14:00 drift held the trend's pullback level, the afternoon push will continue the trend. If the drift broke the morning's structure, expect a reversal. The 15:30–16:00 sub-window is critical for crypto as it aligns with the daily candle close. setup_name: Weekly Open Kill Zone — Sunday/Monday Institutional Entry

Trading the weekly open involves: (1) waiting for the first 1-2 hours to establish direction, (2) entering pullbacks to the weekly open, (3) targeting the weekly pivot levels. setup_name: End-of-Week Close — Friday Profit Taking and Reversal

Crypto Friday close is particularly important — weekend gaps in BTC often fill by Sunday open. This is a counter-trend trader's best window.

setup_name: Asian Range Liquidity Sweep — Smart Money Entry Model

setup_name: Session-based Volatility Compression — Pre-Breakout Accumulation

setup_name: Kill Zone Rejection Scalp — 1-Minute Inside Kill Zone

setup_name: Mid-Session Void — Liquidity Gap Window

setup_name: NYSE Open Momentum Burst — First 30 Minutes

setup_name: Dual Kill Zone Day — London + NY Confluence

setup_name: Diverging Kill Zone Day — London vs NY Conflict

setup_name: Pre-News Position Squaring — 30 Minutes Before Major Data

setup_name: Post-News Momentum Exhaustion — Fade After Initial Spike

Strategy: wait for the 15-minute mark after major news; if price has reversed the spike by >38.2%, enter in the reversal direction with stop beyond the spike extreme. This works because Smart Money uses the news-induced liquidity to fill their real positions. The fake-spike-then-reverse pattern occurs 55-65% of the time on major releases.

setup_name: Session High-Low Breakout Filter — Day Structure Model

setup_name: First Hour Range — Session Direction Indicator

setup_name: Session Transition Failure — False Breakout at Session Change

setup_name: Crypto Weekend Gap Risk — Friday Close to Sunday Open

setup_name: Quarter-End and Month-End Window Dressing — Institutional Rebalancing

Strategy: (1) Identify the quarter's strongest-performing assets — these will see profit-taking into month/quarter end, (2) Identify the quarter's weakest — these will see tax-loss selling or forced liquidation, (3) Expect the OPPOSITE direction in the first week of the new quarter as new money is deployed. For crypto, quarter-ends (especially Q4) often mark major tops or bottoms. The last 2 hours of the last trading day of the quarter (15:00-17:00 EST) see the heaviest rebalancing volume.

setup_name: Session VWAP Alignment — Multi-Timeframe Confirmation
keywords: VWAP, session VWAP, volume weighted average, institutional benchmark, VWAP alignment, multi-timeframe

If all three VWAPs are aligned (e.g., Asian VWAP < London VWAP < NY VWAP for bullish), the trend is strongly confirmed. If they diverge, the market is in rotation. Strategy: only take trades in the direction of VWAP alignment. Price above all VWAPs = longs only. Price below all VWAPs = shorts only. Mixed alignment = range-bound, trade mean-reversion. The VWAP anchor is the most reliable intraday indicator when combined with session filtering.
